la:noun:peroratio.html:
pĕr-ōrātĭo, ōnis, f.
peroro
,
the finishing part, the close or winding up of a speech, the peroration: exstat ejus peroratio, qui epilogus dicitur,: jubent exordiri ... deinde rem narrare ... post autem dividere causam ... Tum alii conclusionem orationis et quasi perorationem collocant: alii jubent, antequam peroretur, digredi, deinde concludere, ac perorare,; ; cf. ; ; .

la:adj:perornatus.html:

la:verb:peroro.html:
pĕr-ōro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to speak from beginning to end, to plead or argue throughout, to harangue at length (class.).
Prop.: QVOM PERORANT AMBO PRAESENTES, Fragm. XII. Tab. ap. : contra tales oratores tantam causam perorare,: a Quinto Hortensio causa est P. Sestii perorata,: et breviter peroratum esse potuit, nihil me commisisse,: jus perorandi,; : tribus horis,; : in Proculas,.—
In partic., to bring a speech to a close, to wind up, conclude, finish: strepitu senatūs coactus est, aliquando perorare,: alii jubent antequam peroretur digredi,: dicta est a me causa et perorata,; ; : brevi,: peroratā narratione,: quoniam satis multa dixi, est mihi perorandum,: de ceteris perorare,.—
In gen., to bring to an end; to conclude, finish a thing: res illo die non peroratur, dimittitur judicium,: de quā cum dixero totum hoc crimen decumanum perorabo,, § 154; .—
To persuade: vultus adest precibus faciesque incesta perorat,.—
(Acc. to oro, II. B.) To pray, to bring a prayer to an end: et hic quidem ita peroravit,.
